q-107857.name: Question 3
q-107857.worked_solution:
To evaluate the gamma function at multiples of one-half, we use the following recursive formula:

$$
Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z),\,Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{\pi }
$$

So, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\pi }\,Γ(\frac{7}{2}) & =\sqrt{\pi }\cdot \frac{5}{2}Γ(\frac{5}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{\pi }\cdot \frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}Γ(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{\pi }\cdot \frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}Γ(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{\pi }\cdot \frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi } \\  & =\frac{15\pi }{8}\end{aligned}
$$

q-107859.name: Question 4
q-107859.worked_solution:
To evaluate the gamma function at multiples of one-half, we use the following recursive formula:

$$
Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z),\,Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{\pi }
$$

So, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}Γ(\frac{5}{2}) & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}\cdot \frac{3}{2}Γ(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot Γ(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

q-107861.name: Question 5
q-107861.worked_solution:
To evaluate the gamma function at multiples of one-half, we use the following recursive formula:

$$
Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z),\,Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{\pi }
$$

So, we have the following:

$$
Γ(\frac{3}{2})=\frac{1}{2}Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi },
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ(\frac{5}{2})=\frac{3}{2}Γ(\frac{3}{2})=\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi }=\frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
2\,Γ(\frac{5}{2})+Γ(\frac{3}{2})=2\cdot \frac{3}{4}\sqrt{\pi }+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi }=2\sqrt{\pi }.
$$

q-107861.html:
Question 5
?

2Γ(52)+Γ(32)=

a
2π
b
8π
c
3π
d
4π
e
6π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To evaluate the gamma function at multiples of one-half, we use the following recursive formula:

Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z),Γ(12)=π

So, we have the following:

Γ(32)=12Γ(12)=12π,

Γ(52)=32Γ(32)=32⋅12π=34π

Therefore,

2Γ(52)+Γ(32)=2⋅34π+12π=2π.
